newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares firm at noon as A shares soar.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares firm at noon as A shares soar.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share index rose at midday on Monday, led by a surge in the domestic A share market, brokers said.
The B share index added 4.70 points or 3.07 percent to 157.77, while the A share index jumped 19.07 points or 4.30 percent to 462.98.
B share turnover reached HK$39.6 million, with turnover on the A share market hitting 3.7 billion yuan.
"The A shares advanced due to the absence of new crackdown measures over the weekend and B shares followed suit," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Beijing last month announced a string of policies aimed at cooling down the country's overheated stock markets which sent share prices down sharply.
Investors generally expect Beijing to refrain from clamping down on the markets in the last month before the British colony of Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, brokers said.
"Any new anti-speculation policies announced this month should be rather mild," the Guotai analyst said.
In the B share market, Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Co Ltd was the most actively traded counter on volume of 2.2 million shares. The stock climbed HK$0.23 to HK$6.76.
In the A share market, large capitalisation Shenzhen Development Bank gained 0.56 yuan to 34.20 yuan on the session's heaviest volume of 10.6 million shares.
